official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship includes exemption from fees for education at NAWA preparatory courses or at public universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that have a framework agreement with NAWA. At private universities the fee exemption is at the university's discretion and financial arrangements are agreed individually with the scholarship holder.
benefits: Monthly scholarship of PLN 2,500 paid for a maximum of 12 months in the academic year (maximum 5 months in the winter semester and 7 in the summer semester)
Exemption from fees for education at NAWA preparatory courses or at public universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education with a framework agreement with NAWA
Lump sum for international travel costs related to coming to Poland to undertake education, a paid-out allowance of PLN 2,500
For scholarship holders on the 'preparatory course and second-cycle studies' path, a one-year NAWA preparatory course is funded on scholarship terms
For scholarship holders on the English path, a course in Polish language and culture is included
eligibility: The offer is addressed to citizens of the listed eligible countries, which include Albania, Angola, Argentina, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Georgia, India, Indonesia, Iraq, Iran, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Kenya, Kosovo, Lebanon, Mexico, Moldova, Mongolia, Montenegro, Nigeria, North Macedonia, Palestine, Papua New Guinea, Peru, the Philippines, Rwanda, Senegal, Serbia, Tanzania and others

Applicants must meet the citizenship, education and language criteria at the time of recruitment, and must hold a degree by 15 July 2026 where the country does not have a common two-cycle study system

The programme supports full-time second-cycle studies in Polish or English at universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that have concluded a framework agreement with NAWA
requirements: Registration in the university's online systems within the deadlines specified by the university, in line with the rules applicable to international candidates
Documents certifying knowledge of the language of instruction at a level of at least B2 must be submitted during the admission process

The applicant selects one of the scholarship paths at the application stage: the Polish language path (preparatory course plus second-cycle studies, or second-cycle studies in Polish without a preparatory course) or the English path (second-cycle studies in English plus a course in Polish language and culture)
During the admission process the university may require legalized or apostilled documents
documents: Application form submitted through the NAWA IT system
Language certificate at a level of at least B2 in the language of instruction, drawn from NAWA's List of Recognized Polish Language Certificates or List of Recognized English Language Certificates
Documents from previous studies, as required by the university's international admission process
selection_criteria: Meeting the citizenship, education and language criteria at the time of recruitment
Registration within the university's online admission deadlines, in accordance with the rules for international candidates
Choice of one of the two scholarship paths and fulfilment of its specific requirements
coverage: Monthly scholarship of PLN 2,500, paid for a maximum of 12 months in the academic year
Exemption from fees for education at NAWA preparatory courses or at public universities under the supervision of the Minister of Science and Higher Education with a framework agreement with NAWA
Lump sum for international travel costs related to coming to Poland to undertake education
The scholarship is paid through the unit conducting the preparatory course or the university where the scholarship holder is studying

Submit the scholarship application through the NAWA IT system, selecting the scholarship path
Prepare to submit documents certifying knowledge of the language of instruction at a level of at least B2 during the admission process
official.application_route: Apply through the NAWA online IT system and register with the chosen university's online systems within its admissions deadlines. The scholarship agreement must be concluded no later than 45 days from the date it is made available in the NAWA IT system.
official.study_mode: Full-time second-cycle studies in Polish or English
official.citizenship_residency: Citizenship of one of the countries eligible to participate in the programme; the programme supports the socio-economic development of developing countries by raising the level of education and professional qualifications of citizens of countries eligible to participate in the programme.
official.international_eligibility: This is an international scholarship aimed at citizens of the listed developing countries outside Poland, and it is designed to support their socio-economic development through education in Poland.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any second-cycle (Master's) programme offered by a university supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that has concluded a framework agreement with NAWA; attachments list the institutions that have concluded a framework agreement.
official.duration: One academic year of studies, preceded where applicable by a one-year NAWA preparatory course; the scholarship is paid for a maximum of 12 months in the academic year
official.description: The Banach NAWA Scholarship Programme is financed from the state budget earmarked reserve for development cooperation and aims to support the socio-economic development of developing countries by raising the level of education and professional qualifications of citizens of countries eligible to participate in the programme by offering scholarships for undertaking second-cycle studies in Poland. The programme enables full-time second-cycle studies in Polish or English, provides exemption from education fees at public universities, precedes Polish-language studies with a NAWA-funded one-year preparatory course, and offers a monthly scholarship of PLN 2,500, a lump sum for international travel costs of PLN 2,500, and immersion in Polish language and culture. According to NAWA's announcement schedule, the most recent call is no. 16/2026 of 13 April 2026, for studies or a preparatory course from the winter semester 2026/27.
official.program_type: Government scholarship for international students at Master's level
official.english_requirement: English at a minimum level of B2 to begin second-cycle studies in English, or Polish at a minimum level of B2 to begin second-cycle studies in Polish; certificates must come from NAWA's List of Recognized English or Polish Language Certificates.

not_confirmed: research_requirement: the programme is for taught second-cycle studies and NAWA publishes no research requirement, so this is left null
study_mode full-time is published by NAWA, so a null is not used there; no part-time variant is offered
The full list of eligible countries is truncated on the programme page; the call announcement lists them in full and the count is not stated

applicant_utility.summary: The Banach scholarship is one of the few international Master's awards that genuinely covers the full package: PLN 2,500 a month for up to twelve months in the academic year, free tuition at the Polish public universities that have a framework agreement with NAWA, a PLN 2,500 one-off travel sum, and a funded year of Polish language study if you take the Polish-language path. The application itself is two-tracked: you apply both through the NAWA IT system and register in your chosen university's own online system, and the university's own admission deadlines govern when you must do the latter. You must choose your path at application stage, so decide early whether you will do a year of Polish before starting, or take the English path with the Polish language and culture course.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A citizen of one of the eligible developing countries who wants a tuition-free Master's degree at a Polish public university, has or can obtain B2 in Polish or English, and is comfortable living in Poland for up to two years.
application_readiness_checklist: Choose your scholarship path first: Polish language path (preparatory course plus second-cycle studies, or studies without the course) or English path (studies in English plus a Polish language and culture course)
Identify a university supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that has a framework agreement with NAWA, and check its own online admission deadlines
Book a B2 certificate from NAWA's List of Recognized English or Polish Language Certificates well before the call opens, because it must be produced during admission
Arrange legalization or apostille of your prior-academic documents, since the university may require them
Conclude the scholarship agreement within 45 days of it being made available in the NAWA IT system, and submit an annual report by 31 October each year
common_rejection_risks: Missing the university's own registration deadlines, which sit before the scholarship result and govern the admission process
Failing to document B2 in the language of instruction at admission
Assuming the tuition exemption applies at private universities: it is at the university's discretion and agreed individually
Being in a country whose group deadline was moved earlier than the general date, in which case applications submitted after that deadline are not considered
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs in Poland are above PLN 2,500 a month in Warsaw, and the travel lump sum is a one-off payment that covers arriving in Poland only; accommodation, insurance, visa and study materials are not part of the package. At a private university, tuition itself would be an out-of-pocket cost.
document_audit: The B2 language certificate must come from NAWA's published list of recognised certificates, so a local test result may not qualify
Legalization or apostille of educational documents should be started early, because universities may require them at admission
alerts: The current call no. 16/2026 closed on 8 May 2026 at 3:00 p.m.; watch NAWA's Banach call-for-proposals page for the next edition
NAWA states it reserves the right to change the amount of funds and not to use the full allocation
At public universities the programme enables free education, but the treatment of prior academic coverage at private universities should be agreed with the university accepting the applicant
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online through the NAWA IT system within the call window, register with the university's own online system within its deadlines, produce a recognised B2 language certificate at admission, then sign the scholarship agreement within 45 days of it being made available.

official.deadline_central_display: 15 May 2026, 3:00:00 p.m. official time in Poland (call no. 9/2026, closed)
official.deadline_note: Call no. 9/2026 of 13 February 2026. The call runs from 1 February 2027 to 31 December 2030, with individual projects of no less than 6 and no more than 24 months starting between 1 February 2027 and 1 December 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2026 call (no. 9/2026 of 13 February 2026) for projects starting in 2027
official.status_note: The Ulam NAWA 2026 call closed on 15 May 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Polish time; applications may only be submitted in electronic form via the Agency's IT system at programs.nawa.gov.pl.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Funding covers the Principal Investigator's remuneration, up to PLN 17,000 per month for full-time employment including employer costs, and a task allowance of up to PLN 1,200 per month for the Inviting Person; tuition fees are not among the eligible costs.
benefits: Employment of a foreign researcher in a Polish higher education or research institution for a period from 6 to 24 months
Remuneration for the Principal Investigator, up to a maximum of PLN 17,000 per month for full-time employment, with amounts including employer costs (gross gross)
Remuneration for the Inviting Person in the form of a task allowance, up to a maximum of PLN 1,200 per month
Maximum funding for a project of PLN 436,800, settled on the basis of actual expenses incurred

A simplified track for applicants who, together with the Principal Investigator, received the Seal of Excellence certificate under MSCA PF-EF or the Accolade of Excellence certificate under MSCA4Ukraine, in which the European certificates act as a binding verification of quality and the remaining requirements for the Principal Investigator do not apply
eligibility: Eligible applicants are entities referred to in Article 7 paragraph 1 points 1, 2 and 4-7 of the Act of 20 July 2018 on Higher Education and Science, which are the institutions that will be employing the Principal Investigator

As a result of the aggression of the Russian Federation against Ukraine, natural persons who are citizens of the Russian Federation, as well as institutions and other entities based in the territory of the Russian Federation, are excluded from participation
Polish citizens may constitute up to 10% of the Principal Investigators under the Programme
There is no limit to the number of applications submitted by a host institution, provided each application indicates a different Principal Investigator
requirements: The Principal Investigator must hold at least a doctoral degree or an equivalent degree obtained abroad at the time of the application deadline; researchers who have obtained the degree but have not yet received the diploma are also considered eligible

The Principal Investigator must be employed at a foreign university or foreign scientific or research centre, or the last employment there must have ended after 31 August 2025; employment is not required for persons who obtained a doctoral degree after 31 August 2025
In the 3 years before the application deadline the Principal Investigator must not have worked or studied in Poland, nor stayed in Poland continuously for longer than 3 months

The Principal Investigator must have at least 3 achievements in the 5 years before the call deadline, taken from publications as main author in English in journals listed in Scopus, SCIE, SSCI or A&HCI, a peer-reviewed scientific monograph in English, publications in English in peer-reviewed CORE-indexed conference proceedings indexed in DBLP, publications in English in peer-reviewed materials from international conferences indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection or Scopus, or, for representatives of art sciences, confirmation of presenting the work in a foreign institution or academic centre or receiving an award in an international competition

The host institution must implement the principles of the European Charter for Researchers, including providing office and laboratory space and research equipment, administrative and financial support, support in applying for national and international research grants, and support in obtaining required consents and permits
The host institution must conclude a full-time employment contract with the Principal Investigator and ensure that the Principal Investigator resides in Poland during the project
documents: Power of attorney for the person submitting the application to represent the applicant, in Polish, using the template provided in the appendix to the Call
A scan of the document confirming that the Principal Investigator is a PhD holder, with official translation into English where the original is in a language other than English or Polish
Invitation of the Principal Investigator by the host institution, signed by the Inviting Person, on the invitation template attached to the Call announcement

A copy of the documents confirming that the Principal Investigator worked as a researcher outside Poland (a certificate from the HR department or a certificate issued by a person representing the employer's institution, with the name of the position and period of employment), in English
Copies of the three required achievements of the Principal Investigator from the last five years, counted from the beginning of 2021

For the special track: an electronic version of the application submitted under the MSCA PF-EF or MSCA4Ukraine programme, the reviews obtained from its evaluation, and an electronic version of the award certificate
selection_criteria: Applications undergo formal assessment first, to determine whether the application is complete and formally meets the requirements of the Call Announcement
Merit-based assessment consists of three stages: initial assessment by the Team of Experts, assessment by two External Reviewers, and final assessment by the Team of Experts
Applications not recommended by the Team of Experts at the initial stage are not submitted for further assessment
coverage: Remuneration for the Principal Investigator, up to PLN 17,000 per month for full-time employment, including employer costs
Task allowance for the Inviting Person, up to PLN 1,200 per month
The project is settled on the basis of actual expenses incurred; the maximum funding for a project is PLN 436,800
application_method: The host institution submits the application electronically through the NAWA IT system at programs.nawa.gov.pl, selecting either Ulam 2026 or Ulam 2026 special track
The application must be completed in English; applications prepared in Polish are disregarded
The Principal Investigator may be included in only one application in the call, and where multiple applications are submitted with the same Principal Investigator only the most recent is assessed
Power of attorney must be prepared in Polish even though the application itself is in English
official.application_route: Electronic submission only, via the Polish National Agency for Academic Exchange's IT system at programs.nawa.gov.pl, in English, with Polish power of attorney and the attachments listed in the call.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to researchers of any nationality, including Polish scientists working permanently abroad, subject to the exclusion of citizens and institutions of the Russian Federation and the rule that Polish citizens may constitute up to 10% of the Principal Investigators.
official.international_eligibility: The programme is open to specialists from abroad regardless of age, discipline or country of origin, including Polish scientists working permanently abroad; the host institution in Poland is the applicant.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The programme is open to all fields of science; representatives of arts are eligible provided the activities planned are of a scientific nature.
official.research_requirement: The Principal Investigator joins the research activity of the Polish institution, particularly research projects and didactic activity, and must be able to carry out the project, including research and teaching. Eligible activities include employment of the researcher in Polish higher education and science institutions, support from the Inviting Person, and creating conditions for completing a postdoctoral internship, conducting research, and obtaining materials for research or scientific publications; employment may also include didactic activity.
official.duration: Employment of between 6 and 24 months, with project start dates between 1 February 2027 and 1 December 2027, inside a programme running from 1 February 2027 to 31 December 2030
official.description: The Ulam NAWA Programme is an institutional programme that aims at increasing the internationalisation of Polish universities and scientific institutions by allowing them to invite outstanding scientists from abroad to strengthen the scientific potential of Polish higher education and research institutions by joining in their research activities, particularly research projects and didactic activity. It provides opportunity to employ foreign researchers for a period from 6 to 24 months, with funding that includes remuneration for the Principal Investigator and for the Inviting Person. According to NAWA's announcement, the call is no. 9/2026 of 13 February 2026. The programme is implemented from 1 February 2027 to 31 December 2030, and the total amount of funds allocated for the implementation of the Programme is PLN 22 million.
official.program_type: Government institutional grant for hiring foreign researchers in Poland
official.english_requirement: The application must be completed in English. Applications prepared in Polish are disregarded. The language of the required attachments is specified in the call: the power of attorney is in Polish, the PhD document must have an official translation into English where the original is in another language, the invitation is attached to the call announcement, the employment certificate is in English, and the achievements from the last five years are publications in English.

not_confirmed: living_cost_coverage: the funding is structured as employment remuneration and a task allowance, and the call does not describe it as covering living costs separately, so this field is left null rather than asserted
The exact maximum number of months for which the PLN 436,800 cap corresponds is not stated as a formula in the call

Payment scheme A and reporting scheme A are named in the call but the underlying details sit in the Regulations for Institutional Programmes for Researchers, an attachment that was not opened in this verification

The call is no. 9/2026 of 13 February 2026, closing 15 May 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Polish time. A formatting error in the source PDF text was corrected here: the programme period is 1 February 2027 to 31 December 2030.

applicant_utility.summary: The Ulam programme is not one you apply for as an individual researcher: the applicant is the Polish institution that will employ you, and your job is to find that host institution and an Inviting Person there who wants to bring you in. If you are a researcher holding a doctorate, currently or recently employed outside Poland, with three English-language publications in Scopus, Web of Science or similar over the past five years, you are the kind of candidate a Polish host can build an application around. The financial ceiling is significant: PLN 17,000 a month gross towards your salary, PLN 1,200 a month for your Polish Inviting Person, and PLN 436,800 in total, enough for a two-year contract. Note that Russians and Russia-based institutions are excluded entirely, and Polish citizens can occupy only 10% of the slots, so this is genuinely a mobility scheme for foreign researchers.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A doctoral-level researcher employed at a non-Polish university or research centre who wants a full-time research and teaching post in Poland, and who has or can find a Polish host institution willing to act as applicant.
application_readiness_checklist: Find a Polish higher education or research institution that will employ you and nominate an Inviting Person there to support you locally
Check the 3-year Polish rule: no work or study in Poland, and no continuous stay longer than 3 months, in the 3 years before the deadline
Confirm the doctoral degree is awarded or already awarded by the deadline, since the diploma need not yet be issued but the degree must be held

Assemble three qualifying achievements from the last five years, all of the kind listed: English-language main-author journal publications in Scopus, SCIE, SSCI or A&HCI, a peer-reviewed monograph, or indexed conference output
Prepare the power of attorney in Polish, since only that part of the file is in Polish while the application is in English
Obtain an HR certificate or employer certificate confirming your position abroad, in English
Submit only one application in the call, because duplicate applications for the same Principal Investigator are reduced to the most recent
common_rejection_risks: Applying directly instead of through a Polish host institution, which makes the application ineligible at formal assessment
Being a citizen of the Russian Federation, or being based in a Russian institution, which excludes both you and the host
Having worked or studied in Poland within the 3 years before the deadline, which fails the mobility requirement
Failing to arrange a full-time employment contract, which the host institution must conclude with the Principal Investigator
Submitting the application in Polish, which the call disregards, or missing the Polish power of attorney
Not ensuring the Principal Investigator will reside in Poland during the project
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The funding covers employment remuneration and the Inviting Person's task allowance and is settled on actual expenses; travel, relocation and living costs outside employment are not separate budget lines. If employment is made part-time, the financing is reduced proportionally.
document_audit: The power of attorney must be in Polish, using the template in the appendix to the Call
The PhD document needs an official English translation if the original is in another language
The host institution must provide practical support under the European Charter for Researchers, including office and laboratory space, so this should be settled before submission
alerts: A simplified special track exists for MSCA Seal of Excellence and MSCA4Ukraine Accolade holders, in which NAWA treats the European certificate as binding verification of quality and waives the remaining Principal Investigator requirements
The programme runs from 1 February 2027 to 31 December 2030, with projects starting between 1 February 2027 and 1 December 2027, and NAWA reserves the right to change the PLN 22 million allocation
If you want to contact NAWA directly, the call lists the Department for Programmes for Scientists with contact details published on the programme pages
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The Polish host institution submits the application electronically at programs.nawa.gov.pl in English, selecting Ulam 2026 or Ulam 2026 special track, with the Polish power of attorney, the PhD scan with English translation, the signed invitation, the English employment certificate and copies of the three achievements attached.
